Question: Taiwan’s air defense density is so high, how can mainland China break through?
Answer: Ask Israel. The distance between Israel and Iran is >1,700km. There are multiple countries between them, and plenty of seawater. Iran also broadcast its intention to attack Israel well in advance. The US (and others) were on full alert waiting to shoot down Iranian munitions. There were Aegis systems on USN ships, land-based THAAD and Patriot batteries, airborn fighters guided by awacs and Israel’s own Iron Dome forming a multi-layered defense system with over 1,500km of strategic depth. More than $1b in munitions was expended to counter the Iranian assault, which totaled a measly ~200 drones and cruise/hypersonic missiles. That’s a far more comprehensive and extravagant air defense than Taiwan can possibly field, if only because the mainland is less than 200km from Taiwan’s coast and the island a mere 400 km long and 150 km across with no strategic depth to speak of. And yet, Iranian hypersonic missiles got through and hit one of the most well-protected and sensitive airbases in the Negev housing the F-35, to prove a point. These weren’t even the most advanced and potent missiles in the Iranian arsenal. Now, is anyone willing to bet the Chinese don’t have better missiles in both quality and quantity? You only need to destroy air defenses once, and China has tactical rocket artillery that can rain fire from the sky 24.7 to mop up or suppress the enemy. And we have not included the air force and navy, which have bombs and missiles aplenty. Good luck.

Question: Why do military analysts insist that Russia would steamroll NATO despite their inability to defeat Ukraine?
Answer: Heard of the Vietnam War? Now, how did a war in Vietnam cause Laos, a neutral country in the conflict, to become one of the most bombed nations in the history of warfare? American munitions dropped half a century ago continue to maim and kill Laotians today. Answer that, and one will be more than halfway through the answer for the question posed. In a conflict escalation, there are no safe havens anymore. Supply lines will be targeted. Long range sensor support will be targeted. Foreign airfields from which flights originate will be targeted. Belarus may open a second front. Tactical nukes will enter the battlefield. Russia has mobilized over a million men, NATO hasn’t. Russians see this conflict as an existential threat to the Russian nation. NATO doesn’t. Russians have give the mandate to Putin to pursue victory. NATO haven’t. It is a question of attitudes—which side has the resolve and grasp of reality. The West does not need to fight Russia, whereas Russia has no choice but to fight the West. As Sun Tzu said, “know yourself and your enemy, and you will not lose in a hundred battles”.

Name: Bill Chen
Question: I'm from India. How can India and China resolve it's border issue without blaming each other for a greater good of Asian dominance. Only positive comments from both sides please?
Answer: Ever since Jawaharlal’s overreach, China has stringently kept to the negotiated bargain struck through numerous rounds of talks. That includes no firearms on border patrols, and mutual retreat from the disputed border, creating a no-man’s land buffer. Unfortunately, India decided to unilaterally upset the hard-won status quo by introducing settlers, and upgrading connectivity, making inroads into no-man’s land. The pace has accelerated alarmingly in the 21st century. The Chinese mirrored Indian development, but managed to do so at a faster clip than the Indians, particularly east of the vulnerable chicken’s neck. This caused the Indians to break longstanding protocol, when armed Indian troops entered Doklam in 2017 to stop Chinese troops from constructing a road. That could have easily led to war. Provocation been escalating for years along many parts of the India-China behavior, and isn’t confined to the Mcmahon line. India needs a strong leader to walk back on Jawaharlal’s legacy, and admit the strategic overreach. Unfortunately, his status as the father of Indian democracy prevents the polity from disavowing its past, just like the Chrysanthemum throne’s iron grip on Japanese history. I see no way out, and I expect the border issue to be milked for political effect periodically, like what we witnessed during covid. China is willing to sit down and negotiate any time.

Question: USA is to withdraw US troops in Luchu (Okinawa) to Guam & Hawaii starting Dec 2024. At first, 4000 (40%) troops. Also withdraw some from Japan mainland. Is USA handing over the 1st island chain to China? Is China's military so strong that US military must withdraw?
Answer: Well, Okinawa is too close to the mainland. It lacks the strategic depth necessary for a LAYERED missile defense. Yes, Okinawa’s location makes it an ideal strike platform to threaten targets on the mainland, but no country can hope to outgun China at its doorstep. In other words, Okinawa is not survivable, in the current missile calculus. Guam, being thousands of km further, has more warning time and the luxury of strategic depth to deploy a triple layer defense of Aegis, THAAD and Patriot, along with dispersal of force in fortified bunkers on separate islands. The Americans are betting on a fortified keystone to turn the Western Pacific into no-man’s land, operating destroyer and submarine wolf-packs to threaten shipping (both naval and air) in the Western Pacific. That’s how I read the massive program to enlarge both fleets, in tandem with the formation of the Quad and Aukus. Okinawa may be turned into another Philippines, with marines manning Typhon systems with missiles that can hit targets over 2,000km away, giving the US an edge in a surprise strike while risking relatively few men and assets.
